/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
from pypdf import PdfReader
out=Path('tmp/pdfs')
out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
print('PAGES',len(r.pages))
print('METADATA',r.metadata)
for i,p in enumerate(r.pages,1):
    text=p.extract_text(extraction_mode='layout')
    (out/f'page-{i:02d}.txt').write_text(text)
    print(f'PAGE {i}: {len(text)} chars')
(out/'manuscript.txt').write_text('\\n\\n'.join(f'PAGE {i}\\n'+(out/f'page-{i:02d}.txt').read_text() for i in range(1,len(r.pages)+1)))
PY"

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
p=Path('tmp/pdfs')
paths=[p/'manuscript.txt',p/'detail-page-07.png']
paths += [p/f'page-{i:02d}.{ext}' for i in range(1,17) for ext in ('png','txt')]
for path in paths:
    if path.exists():
        path.unlink()
p.rmdir()
print('Removed temporary text extracts and page renders; manuscript unchanged.')
PY"

strengths: AiT offers a potentially useful combination of compact explicit memory, sparse writes across image patches, and associative retrieval. Its integration as an additional ViT component provides a concrete contribution to visual representation learning.

Table 1 reports meaningful improvements over ViT with matched depth and width. AiT-Small improves CIFAR-10 accuracy from 79.53% to 83.34% and CIFAR-100 from 53.19% to 56.30%, while increasing parameters from 14.9M to 15.8M. Improvements also persist in the Base configuration.

The component ablations provide useful evidence. Removing the bottleneck reduces CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 accuracy to 75.40%/46.53%, while replacing Hopfield retrieval with cross-attention yields 81.03%/54.96%. Memory initialization, temperature experiments, and slot visualizations offer additional diagnostics.
weaknesses: The reported gains are promising, but consequential uncertainties about the algorithm and evaluation protocol currently favor rejection. Sections 4.1–4.2 pool patches across minibatches and update evolving memory, without specifying whether memory is frozen, reset, or updated during testing, or how gradients propagate across memory updates. Evaluation batch-size/composition controls and an ablation of cross-sample pooling are absent. Consequently, the dependence of predictions on other evaluation samples and memory history remains unresolved.

Hopfield retrieval is insufficiently specified. Equations (7)–(8) provide an energy and an argmin, but no implemented update rule, iteration count, stopping criterion, or differentiation strategy. These choices affect both accuracy and computational cost. Furthermore, the standard continuous-Hopfield update is a softmax-weighted memory read, so the claimed fundamental distinction from attention is overstated; the contribution is better supported as an architectural combination.

The complexity claims do not follow from the stated computation. Section 4.2 computes all M-by-BN attention scores before applying top-k; input projections also depend on embedding dimension E. Retaining conventional self-attention preserves quadratic dependence on per-image patch count in the complete model. Thus, fixed bottleneck capacity does not establish input-size/dimension-invariant computation. Parameter counts alone, without runtime, activation-memory, or scaling measurements, do not substantiate the broader efficiency claims.

The proposed balance loss has an unresolved differentiation issue. In Equation (5), the load count uses an indicator of positive attention: for the previously defined unmasked softmax it is constant, while after hard top-k masking it has zero gradient almost everywhere. No surrogate gradient is described. Figures 8–9 show diversity increasing during training, but lack a matched experiment without the balance loss, so they do not establish its causal contribution or functional specialization of the priors.

The demonstrated benefits are task-dependent. On relational Sort-of-CLEVR questions, AiT obtains 67.74%, below Coordination's 73.43% and CNN+RN's 81.07%, despite its strong non-relational result. This limits the evidence for improved relational representations. The main accuracy tables also omit variability despite reporting three-run means, leaving uncertainty around the smaller improvements.

A separate, readily correctable reporting problem is the learning-rate discrepancy: Section 5.1 specifies 1e-5, whereas Table 6 specifies 1e-4. The validation protocol used for the reported grid search is also unspecified. These reporting issues compound reproducibility concerns but would not independently determine rejection.
